koinonia:verdict/55.koinonia:why: Ragin's necessity consistency is Σmin(x,y)/Σy for X necessary for Y; written as Y⊆X. Ratio of sums, so recomputing it at each level is right.

koinonia:verdict/56.koinonia:why: An ordinal invariance level carried up by min is sensible: the combined level is only the weakest level that holds across groups.

koinonia:verdict/57.koinonia:why: A density of residents plus jobs per area aggregates correctly as a ratio of sums; the definition matches the name and unit.

koinonia:verdict/58.koinonia:why: Max across gauges might be intended as worst exposure, but the entry does not say. Days per year cannot be summed, and union days would need recomputation.

koinonia:verdict/59.koinonia:why: Declared kind 'rate' triggers R1 against summing, yet spills/yr counts events and is effectively extensive, so summation across outfalls is sensible; the entry's text conflicts with itself.

koinonia:verdict/60.koinonia:why: Net income per vendor per day is a skewed flow; the median across vendors at street and city scale is a sensible aggregation.

koinonia:verdict/61.koinonia:why: 'decomposable' is not an allowed aggregation. MPI is population-weighted across subgroups, so it should be wmean:population. The household scale is also odd for a headcount ratio.

koinonia:verdict/62.koinonia:why: A network is only as good as its weakest link, so taking the minimum return period upward is defensible. The definition fits the name and the unit.

koinonia:verdict/63.koinonia:why: 'decomposable' is not an allowed aggregation. Theil needs within-group plus between-group terms, so it should be recompute. The definition and the nats unit are otherwise correct.

koinonia:verdict/64.koinonia:why: Gi* z-score is intensive and marked 'recompute', not summed; definition and source are given, so R1, R4 and R5 are satisfied. No checks were supplied to dispute.

koinonia:verdict/69.koinonia:why: A relative shortfall against a planning standard, per facility type, is a dimensionless ratio. Keeping it at one level and not aggregating it is defensible.

koinonia:verdict/70.koinonia:why: Twelve categories at 3–81 each give a range of 36–972, not 0–972. The definition also lists only eight factors, not twelve.

koinonia:verdict/71.koinonia:why: For pedestrians the HCM signal delay is (C − g)²/(2C), so the formula is right. But weighting by trips suits vehicles; pedestrian delay should be weighted by pedestrian crossings.

koinonia:verdict/72.koinonia:why: Conflicts divided by observation hours, summed over sites, is the right pooled rate. The unit and the Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique definition are consistent.

koinonia:verdict/73.koinonia:why: Per-facility-type gap ratio against standards is non-additive; keeping it unaggregated is defensible, and the definition fits name and unit 1.

koinonia:verdict/74.koinonia:why: Summed RHRS category scores give an ordinal score; taking the max along a network flags the worst slope, which is appropriate.

koinonia:verdict/75.koinonia:why: Mean pedestrian wait should be weighted by pedestrians or crossings, not trips. HCM signal delay is (C−g)²/(2C), which matches the definition.

koinonia:verdict/76.koinonia:why: Conflicts per observed hour; summing conflicts over summed hours correctly aggregates the rate, consistent with Swedish TCT.

koinonia:verdict/82.koinonia:why: A length-weighted mean of H/W along street segments is a standard aggregation. The definition matches the name and the dimensionless unit.

koinonia:verdict/83.koinonia:why: A per-project dimensionless ratio, recomputed at its single project scale. The definition fits the name.

koinonia:verdict/84.koinonia:why: Cover at a higher level should be total stock over total daily consumption (ratio-of-sums), not the minimum across sub-units.

koinonia:verdict/85.koinonia:why: Aggregation 'none' breaks no rule; nothing is summed or averaged. The source (Wardman 2004) and the definition are both stated. Listing several scales does not violate R1–R5.

koinonia:verdict/86.koinonia:why: Energy not supplied in MWh per year is an extensive flow total, not an intensive rate; summing across network, city, region is valid. Source and definition are present.

koinonia:verdict/87.koinonia:why: Mean Likert-scale attitude scores weighted by population roll up properly from neighbourhood to city; the definition fits the name and unit.

koinonia:verdict/88.koinonia:why: A ratio of stocks to consumption should aggregate as ratio-of-sums. Taking the minimum understates the reserve of the aggregate unit.

koinonia:verdict/89.koinonia:why: Taking the worst-case maximum is a defensible way to roll up ordinal risk levels, and the definition matches the matrix-based unit.

koinonia:verdict/90.koinonia:why: The mean rating should be weighted by review count, which is the denominator in the definition, not by visitors.

koinonia:verdict/91.koinonia:why: Latent attitude score per resident; a population-weighted mean is a sound way to carry it from neighbourhood to city.

koinonia:verdict/92.koinonia:why: Taking the minimum of days misstates the reserves of a larger unit; it should be ratio-of-sums of stocks over daily consumption.

koinonia:verdict/93.koinonia:why: An ordinal level read from a matrix; taking the maximum, the worst rating, is a defensible conservative way to aggregate upward.

koinonia:verdict/94.koinonia:why: Star means should be weighted by review count, which the definition names; visitors are not reviewers, so the weight is wrong.

koinonia:verdict/95.koinonia:why: A 1–5 Likert score is an ordinal level; R2 forbids averaging it, so a population-weighted mean violates the rule. It should carry the median or not aggregate.

koinonia:verdict/100.koinonia:why: Person-days are additive counts; summing across neighbourhoods to city and region is correct and the definition matches name and unit.

koinonia:verdict/101.koinonia:why: LPI is a site hazard index on 0–100. Carrying the worst case up via max is a defensible conservative choice; the definition matches Iwasaki.

koinonia:verdict/102.koinonia:why: A per-person daily mean is properly aggregated as a population-weighted mean; the definition fits the name and unit.

koinonia:verdict/103.koinonia:why: Individual Likert scores averaged over members, weighted by headcount, give a valid group mean; the definition matches the CQS.

koinonia:verdict/104.koinonia:why: The entry has a 1–4 Likert (ordinal) unit, yet its aggregation is a population-weighted mean. R2 forbids averaging ordinal levels; it allows only the median.

koinonia:verdict/105.koinonia:why: Weekly event counts are extensive; district totals sum to the city total. 'Per week' is a time window, not a ratio, so R1 doesn't apply. Source and definition are stated.

koinonia:verdict/106.koinonia:why: Rate aggregated by max, not summed, so R1 is respected. R2 and R3 do not apply. Source and definition are stated. Unstated intent is not a rule violation.

koinonia:verdict/107.koinonia:why: Decomposable aggregation is population-weighted, not a sum, so R1 is respected. Source and definition are stated. No rule restricts aggregation labels, so the second check invents a rule.

koinonia:verdict/108.koinonia:why: No declared rule lists allowed aggregation values. The Theil index is not summed: the definition gives an exact within-plus-between decomposition. The source and definition are stated, so R1–R5 are met.

koinonia:verdict/109.koinonia:why: The entry is internally inconsistent. It states a 0–972 range from twelve categories scored 3–81 each, which would give 36–972. Its definition also lists only eight factors.

koinonia:verdict/110.koinonia:why: Median is correct for ordinal levels, but the definition adds the BJT J5–J1+ scale, which the stated unit (JLPT N5–N1) does not cover. The entry is internally inconsistent.

koinonia:verdict/111.koinonia:why: Min is not summing an intensive quantity; no median or ordinal involved; source and definition stated. The ratio-of-sums objection invokes no declared rule.

koinonia:verdict/112.koinonia:why: Person-days is an extensive count, not an intensive rate or index; summing up the hierarchy is valid. Source and definition are stated, so R1 does not apply.

koinonia:verdict/113.koinonia:why: The unit is a 1–7 Likert scale, an ordinal level, yet aggregation is a population-weighted mean. R2 forbids averaging ordinal levels; only a median may carry them.
